name: Terminal / character grid
summary: A fixed R x C grid of equal-width cells in which every element is a positioned run of cells, runs are protected or editable, one row-major order governs reading, traversal, and source order, and status and named action keys occupy reserved runs.
tasks: operator workflows moving between fixed screens
notFor: content whose meaning does not depend on position (use a conventional form or list)

semanticRegions.purpose: Names the screen and, where used, its transaction or panel identifier.
Protected context the operator must verify before acting (system, date, user, record key).
Positioned protected text and editable fields for the task.
semanticRegions.html: grid of positioned runs inside a form when any field is editable

semanticRegions.purpose: Dense repeated records with aligned columns.
semanticRegions.html: table (column headers + rows) placed in the grid

semanticRegions.purpose: Validation, error, warning, information, and success messages about the current screen.
Terminal/system state such as input inhibited, waiting, or insert mode.
Named action affordances (Enter, Clear, Reset, PF/F keys, named actions).
semanticRegions.html: group of native buttons with visible names

sourceOrder.rule: Positioned runs appear in ascending row-major order (row x columns + column). Reserved regions keep this rule because they occupy the bottom rows.
sourceOrder.consequence: DOM order, reading order, focus order, and visual order are the same sequence without tabindex.
sourceOrder.exceptions: None inside the grid. Content outside the grid (page chrome) follows normal page order.

recognitionPath: editable fields or the rows being scanned
verificationRegions: protected context values (which record am I on?)
validation and error messages tied to specific fields
amounts, dates, and statuses in repeated rows
consequential action keys (e.g. submit, delete, post)

composition.grid: Explicit integer rows and columns. Reference geometries: 24x80 and 32x80. Other known geometries: 43x80 and 27x132.
composition.cell: Equal advance width of one monospaced character (1ch); row height is one line box. The grid therefore scales with text size, not viewport width.
composition.placement: Every element declares (row, column, length) in 1-based cells. Rendered position equals declared position.
composition.alignment: Labels and values align to shared column positions; repeated-row columns align to fixed column starts; numeric amounts align on their right edge within a fixed-length run.
composition.density: High. Whitespace is expressed as blank cells. Grouping is shown by blank rows, blank columns, rule glyphs, or protected headings, not by proportional spacing.
composition.landmarks: The terminal is one labelled region. Inside it, regions are distinguished by headings, a form, a table, and live regions rather than nested page landmarks.
composition.boundaries: Editable runs have a visible boundary that does not depend on color (bracket glyphs, underscore run, or outline).

navigation.keyboardOrder: Tab/Shift+Tab move through editable fields and then action buttons in row-major order. Arrow-key cell navigation is not required.
navigation.focusOrder: Same as keyboard order; focus is always visible and never entirely obscured by the contained scroller.
navigation.readingOrder: Row-major; protected labels precede the value or field they label.
decisionPoints: PF/F keys: navigate or invoke named functions
Clear: erase and return to an initial state
Reset: local recovery from an inhibited or error state
navigation.exitFromGrid: Tab must be able to leave the terminal region. Wraparound from the last field to the first is optional application behavior, not part of the family.

preservedRelationships: row-major order = source order = focus order = visual order
label precedes and is programmatically associated with its field
protected runs are never focusable form controls unless they are genuine read-only form values
no two runs share a cell
no run crosses the right edge (no row wrap)
message row is associated with the field(s) it describes
action key names are visible text, not color or position alone
status and message regions persist in a fixed location across screens of a workflow

responsive.wide: The grid renders at its natural width (C ch plus padding). Extra viewport width is margin; the grid does not stretch cells or add columns.

narrow.contained: The grid keeps its geometry inside a horizontally scrollable, keyboard-focusable region with an accessible name. The page itself never overflows horizontally. Focus moving to a field scrolls it into view.
narrow.reflow: Opt-in alternative for screens whose positions carry no meaning: runs are presented in source order as a single column; labels stay with fields; action keys wrap. Positions are not preserved.
narrow.choice: Authors must justify contained against WCAG 1.4.10: the exception applies only where two-dimensional layout is required for usage or meaning, and text inside cells must still be readable.

responsive.zoom: At 200% text size the grid grows proportionally and remains contained; no characters are clipped or overlapped. Text-spacing overrides (WCAG 1.4.12) may widen cells; the grid must grow rather than clip.

content.long: Protected text longer than its declared length is an authoring error found by validation. Editable input is limited by maxlength. Long lists are paged (PF7/PF8-style or named actions) or continue in a separately scrollable region; they do not push the action row off the grid.
content.missing: Missing protected values render as an explicit placeholder with text meaning (e.g. 'n/a' or 'not on file'), never as silent blanks that look like zero or empty fields.
content.extreme: Maximum-length values fill their run exactly; amounts at the maximum digit count still fit; an empty repeated-row set shows an explicit empty-state message inside the rows region.
content.localization: Translated labels change length; each label run must be sized for the longest supported translation or the layout must be re-authored per locale. Wide-glyph scripts (CJK) commonly occupy two cells per glyph; the family has no verified rule for them. Right-to-left grids are not researched.

accessibility: Native form controls for editable runs with programmatic labels (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2).
Required, invalid, disabled, and read-only states exposed natively and shown without color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
Messages exposed as status/alert live regions (WCAG 4.1.3).
Visible focus indicator distinct from the stylistic cursor (WCAG 2.4.7, 2.4.11).
Action keys operable as buttons; physical key shortcuts are additive and avoid bare printable characters (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.1.4).
Resize text to 200% and text-spacing overrides without loss (WCAG 1.4.4, 1.4.12).
Forced-colors mode keeps field boundaries, focus, and state glyphs visible.
Reduced motion: any SequentialReveal presents immediately (see behavior definition).

behaviors.summary: Optional visual-only row-major staging of already-present text; immediate under reduced motion; never stages fields, actions, messages, status, or consequential values; any input completes it without being consumed.

required: grid container with declared rows and columns and a narrow-screen strategy
positioned editable field run using native input with label, maxlength, and states
message/status region with severity text or glyph
action-key group presenting key name and label
optional SequentialReveal presentation hook with reduced-motion fallback
profile layer for palette, typeface, boundary glyphs, and cursor treatment

knownGaps.gap: Forma had no character-cell positioning primitive; existing layouts are flow/grid compositions measured in rem, not cells.
No Forma contract ties a field's rendered width to its maximum length in characters.
No Forma contract presents named keyboard actions (key + label) separately from their behavior.
No Forma contract for a staged text reveal with a static fallback.
No contained-scroll viewport contract that is keyboard-focusable and named.
No rule for wide-glyph (two-cell) characters or right-to-left grids.

antiPatterns: Imitating a screenshot with absolutely positioned divs that simulate inputs.
Using tabindex to force an order that source order should express.
Rendering protected values as read-only inputs so they look aligned.
Encoding field state or message severity by color only.
Letting the grid cause page-level horizontal scrolling.
Making information available only after an animation completes.
Describing SequentialReveal, green phosphor, or wraparound Tab as authentic 3270 behavior.

assumptions.text: Users of modern keyboard-first grid applications expect row-major field order.
DOS text-mode, BBS, and modern TUIs share the grid invariants.
The 3270 status line sits below the application rows.
Dense cell-aligned presentation supports expert scanning.
1ch of a monospaced face is a stable cell width across engines and zoom.

verification.check: Every positioned run is within bounds and does not cross the right edge.
No two runs share a cell.
Source order equals row-major order of runs.
Every editable run has a label and a length; its maxlength equals its length.
Protected runs are not focusable form controls.
Tab and Shift+Tab visit editable fields and actions in row-major order.
Rendered cell position equals declared position for 24x80 and 32x80.
No page-level horizontal overflow at 320 and 390 CSS px; the contained region is focusable and named.
At 200% text size no characters are clipped and positions still correspond.
Forced colors keep field boundaries, focus, and state cues visible.
With reduced motion requested, revealed content is present and visible immediately.
Message and state cues are not conveyed by color alone.

narrowRecomposition: contained horizontal scroll preserving the grid by default; opt-in reflow to a single column in source order when positions carry no meaning; never page-level overflow
